title: OpenCV headless constraint does not replace RapidOCR's OpenCV dependency

evidence.quote: This override tells uv to satisfy opencv-python requirements with opencv-python-headless instead.

reasoning: A uv constraint on opencv-python-headless constrains that distribution; it does not alias or satisfy a differently named transitive requirement on opencv-python. Because the metadata also adds opencv-python-headless as a direct dependency, the resolver can still install the GUI opencv-python wheel required by RapidOCR alongside the headless wheel, defeating the stated macOS GUI-lib avoidance and increasing install size/conflict risk.
recommendation: Use a supported dependency strategy that actually removes opencv-python from the resolved environment, or remove the misleading headless override and document that the GUI OpenCV wheel is still installed. Regenerate the lockfile after the metadata change.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Unit tests can pass when both cv2-providing wheels are installed; there is no dependency-tree or lockfile assertion for the intended headless-only environment.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI metadata check that resolves dependencies and fails if opencv-python appears in the lock/tree when the intended base install is headless-only.
minimumFixScope: pyproject.toml dependency/uv configuration and uv.lock regeneration.
